questions.stem: Per this page, why does `swap(int a, int b)` leave the caller's `x` and `y` as they were?

options.text: The method is handed copies of the values, not the variables
options.says: The page says copies of the integers' values are passed, so changing them inside the method does not affect the originals.

options.text: The method is handed the variables, but undoes its changes on return
options.says: The page says the method never receives the variables at all, only copies of their values.

options.text: The method is handed cached `int` objects that other code shares
options.says: The page says only copies of the values are passed; caching plays no part in its explanation.

questions.stem: A method runs `s += " World";` on its `String` parameter `s`. Per this page, what does the caller's own variable hold afterwards?

options.text: The caller's text followed by " World", as the String itself was extended
options.says: The page says a String is immutable, so the method cannot change the object the caller holds.

options.text: A null reference, as the parameter was pointed at another String object
options.says: The page says reassigning a parameter only changes the method's copy; the caller's variable is untouched.

options.text: The caller's text as it was, as only the local parameter was reassigned
options.says: The page says that for an immutable String, s += " World" only reassigns the local parameter.
